pharm: Stabilizes inactivated voltage-gated sodium channels, reducing repetitive neuronal firing and limiting the spread of seizure activity; also relieves neuropathic facial pain.
quick: Epilepsy: start 200 mg twice daily; usual 800-1200 mg/day
Take with food to improve tolerability
Teratogenic (neural tube defects); avoid if possible
CBC, LFTs, sodium, drug levels, skin reactions
summary: Carbamazepine is an iminostilbene anticonvulsant used for partial and generalized tonic-clonic seizures, mixed seizure patterns, trigeminal neuralgia, and (extended-release) acute mania/mixed episodes of bipolar disorder. It carries a boxed warning for serious, sometimes fatal dermatologic reactions (Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis) strongly associated with the HLA-B*1502 allele (common in Asian ancestry), and for aplastic anemia and agranulocytosis. It is a potent CYP3A4 inducer with many drug interactions and can cause hyponatremia.
indications: Partial seizures with complex symptomatology (psychomotor, temporal lobe)
Mixed seizure patterns including the above or other partial/generalized seizures
Acute manic and mixed episodes of bipolar I disorder (extended-release formulation)

dosage.d: Start 200 mg twice daily; increase by up to 200 mg/day weekly
dosage.n: Usual 800-1200 mg/day; max generally 1200 mg/day (up to 1600 mg in some adults)

dosage.d: Start 100 mg twice daily; increase by up to 100 mg/day weekly
Start 100 mg twice daily; increase by up to 200 mg/day as needed
dosage.n: Usual 400-800 mg/day; max 1200 mg/day; taper periodically to reassess

dosage.d: Start 200 mg twice daily; adjust by 200 mg/day

admin: Take with food to reduce gastrointestinal upset
Initiate at low dose and titrate gradually to minimize CNS effects
Do not crush or chew extended-release forms; swallow whole
Do not administer suspension simultaneously with other liquid medications (precipitate formation)
Do not discontinue abruptly in seizure patients (risk of status epilepticus)
moa: Carbamazepine acts mainly by binding to voltage-gated sodium channels in their inactivated state, prolonging inactivation and limiting sustained, high-frequency repetitive neuronal firing. This reduces the propagation of seizure discharges and, in trigeminal neuralgia, decreases ectopic firing in pain pathways. It also has modest effects on calcium and potassium channels and on neurotransmitter release. Its active 10,11-epoxide metabolite contributes to activity and toxicity.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to carbamazepine or tricyclic compounds
Use with or within 14 days of a monoamine oxidase inhibitor
Coadministration with nefazodone or delavirdine (and certain other NNRTIs)
relative: HLA-B*1502 positive patients (high SJS/TEN risk - avoid unless benefit outweighs risk)
monitor: Complete blood count for hematologic toxicity

preg: Carbamazepine can cause fetal harm, including neural tube defects (spina bifida), craniofacial defects, cardiovascular malformations, and developmental delay. Use during pregnancy only if the benefit justifies the risk; supplement folic acid and consider the North American Antiepileptic Drug Pregnancy Registry.
lact: Carbamazepine and its epoxide metabolite are excreted in human milk; breastfeeding may be considered with monitoring of the infant for sedation, poor feeding, jaundice, and hematologic effects.
renal: No major dosage adjustment is required for renal impairment, but use caution; carbamazepine can cause hyponatremia/SIADH and should be used carefully in patients with fluid/electrolyte disorders.
hepatic: Use with caution; carbamazepine is hepatically metabolized and can cause hepatotoxicity. It is contraindicated in severe hepatic disease. Monitor liver function.

major: MAO inhibitors - contraindicated (discontinue MAOI >=14 days before)
CYP3A4 substrates (oral contraceptives, warfarin, direct oral anticoagulants, many others) - carbamazepine induces metabolism, reducing their efficacy
CYP3A4 inhibitors (macrolides, azole antifungals, diltiazem/verapamil, grapefruit) - increase carbamazepine levels and toxicity
Other anticonvulsants and lithium - altered levels and additive neurotoxicity
interactions.food: Take with food; grapefruit juice increases carbamazepine levels.
interactions.diagnostics: May cause leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, hyponatremia, abnormal liver tests, and altered thyroid function tests.

emergency: SJS/TEN with blistering and mucosal involvement

monitoring: Skin reactions and signs of hypersensitivity
HLA-B*1502 (Asian ancestry) and consider HLA-A*3101 before starting
counsel: Stop and seek care urgently for any rash, blistering, mouth sores, or fever - serious skin reactions can occur
Report easy bruising, bleeding, sore throat, fever, mouth ulcers, or extreme tiredness (blood problems)
Do not stop suddenly; this can trigger seizures
This drug can make hormonal birth control less effective - use an additional method
Avoid alcohol; tell your doctor about all other medicines, as interactions are common
pk: Anticonvulsant effect over days; autoinduction over weeks
Initially 25-65 h, falling to 12-17 h with autoinduction
Store at 20-25 C; protect tablets from light and moisture (humidity can cause hardening)
pearls: Boxed warning: SJS/TEN (strongly linked to HLA-B*1502, common in Asian ancestry) and aplastic anemia/agranulocytosis
Test HLA-B*1502 in at-risk Asian patients before starting; avoid if positive
Strong CYP3A4 inducer and autoinducer - levels fall over the first weeks and it lowers many drug levels (including contraceptives)
Watch for hyponatremia/SIADH, especially in the elderly
Avoid in absence/atypical absence and myoclonic seizures, which it can worsen
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as you remember unless it is almost time for the next dose, in which case skip it. Do not take a double dose. Do not stop the medicine on your own.
overdose: Overdose causes neuromuscular disturbances (ataxia, nystagmus, mydriasis, twitching), CNS depression progressing to coma, seizures, cardiac conduction abnormalities and arrhythmias, hypotension, and respiratory depression. There is no specific antidote; treat with supportive care, airway protection, activated charcoal, cardiac and neurologic monitoring, and management of seizures and hypotension. Multiple-dose activated charcoal and hemoperfusion/hemodialysis may aid clearance in severe cases.
